Senses.PreferredTarget: complete command of the single conduct
AlternateTargets: complete command of the single conduct
Senses.Explanation: Huineng uses “complete command of the single conduct” for carrying one straightforward mind without attachment through walking, standing, sitting, and lying down. His Platform Record explicitly rejects immobile sitting and suppression of thoughts as the meaning: that account would make it like insentient things and an obstruction to the Way. Huineng first defines it as “at all times, while walking, standing, sitting, and lying down, constantly carry a straightforward mind” (於一切時中，行住坐臥，常行直心), and then as carrying a straightforward mind “without attachment to anything” (於一切法上，無有執著). The Patriarchal Hall Collection preserves the parallel definition: “in every place, walking, standing, sitting, and lying down, all is one straightforward mind; this is the site of the Way, this is the pure land” (於一切處行住坐臥，皆一直心，即是道場，即是淨土). Huineng's rejected account says that sitting without moving and suppressing thoughts is “complete command of the single conduct”; he answers that this is “the same as insentient things” and “a condition obstructing the Way” (同無情，却是障道因緣). Qisong's praise of another Platform edition gives a distinct formulation within the same named compound: “the single aspect of the realm of things” (法界一相), under which “although the many good acts differ, all are made correct in a single conduct” (萬善雖殊，皆正於一行).
Senses.Note: The English translates the final two graphs as “complete command,” as required by the termbase standard; they are not left as an unexplained religious loanword. The direct Huineng definitions and corrective passage are primary. Later lamp witnesses independently preserve the same four-posture and straightforward-mind wording but are historically dependent retellings, so validation rests on multiple allowlisted texts while that dependence is stated.

Occurrences.Kwic: 一行三昧者，於一切時中，行、住、坐、臥，常行直心是。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In the early Platform Record, whose full title is The Supreme Great-Vehicle Scripture of the Southern School's Sudden Teaching, Spoken by Sixth Patriarch Huineng at Dafan Monastery in Shaozhou (南宗頓教最上大乘摩訶般若波羅蜜經六祖惠能大師於韶州大梵寺施法壇經), Huineng directly defines the phrase across the four postures.

Occurrences.Kwic: 但行直心，於一切法上，無有執著，名一行三昧。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In The Supreme Great-Vehicle Scripture of the Southern School's Sudden Teaching, Spoken by Sixth Patriarch Huineng at Dafan Monastery in Shaozhou (南宗頓教最上大乘摩訶般若波羅蜜經六祖惠能大師於韶州大梵寺施法壇經), Huineng gives a second direct definition: straightforward mind without attachment to anything.

Occurrences.Kwic: 迷人著法相，執一行三昧，直言坐不動，除妄不起心，即是一行三昧。若如是，此法同無情，却是障道因緣。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In The Supreme Great-Vehicle Scripture of the Southern School's Sudden Teaching, Spoken by Sixth Patriarch Huineng at Dafan Monastery in Shaozhou (南宗頓教最上大乘摩訶般若波羅蜜經六祖惠能大師於韶州大梵寺施法壇經), Huineng rejects unmoving sitting and thought suppression as a definition, comparing that account to insentient things.

Occurrences.Kwic: 一行三昧者，於一切處行住坐臥，皆一直心，即是道場，即是淨土。此之名為一行三昧。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Patriarchal Hall Collection (祖堂集) records Huineng directly defining the phrase as one straightforward mind through all four postures, the site of the Way, and the pure land.

Occurrences.Kwic: 若於一切處行住坐臥。純一直心不動道場真成淨土。名一行三昧。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Jingde Record of the Lamp (景德傳燈錄), in Huineng's section, records Huineng defining complete command of the single conduct as maintaining a pure, straightforward mind everywhere while walking, standing, sitting, and lying down; Wuxiang is not the speaker.

Occurrences.Kwic: 一行三昧者，法界一相之謂也。謂萬善雖殊，皆正於一行者也。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In the Praise of the Platform Scripture within the Platform Scripture of the Sixth Patriarch (六祖大師法寶壇經), the byline names the Song master Qisong as composer. Qisong, not Huineng, defines complete command of the single conduct here as the single aspect of the realm of things and the many good acts made correct in one conduct.
